note: Liver-directed AAV-FVIII gene therapies (valoctocogene, giroctocogene, SPK-8011, BAX 888) and VWF-independent protein replacement (efanesoctocog alfa) were taken to patients on F8-knockout mice plus cynomolgus macaques, while hemophilia A dogs were the field's durability and tolerance model.

engagement.note: AAV2 heavy/light-chain FVIII vectors gave dose-dependent, therapeutic-to-supraphysiologic plasma FVIII after portal-vein injection in F8-knockout mice.
engagement.quote: After intraportal vein injection of these vectors in hemophilia-A mice, therapeutic to superphysiologic levels of active FVIII were achieved in plasma in a dose-dependent manner.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only (paywalled Blood paper); proxy opening entry for the F8-knockout mouse, which predates 2003 for FVIII protein work.
engagement.judgement: Sibling AAV2 vector, not a member product; the F8-knockout mouse is the common pharmacology model for every member and opens the track here.

engagement.note: Efanesoctocog alfa (BIVV001) held FVIII in the normal range for 4 days in patients, the sustained-activity profile mice and monkeys showed.

engagement.quote: After the injection of BIVV001 in the higher-dose group, the mean factor VIII level was in the normal range (≥51%) for 4 days and 17% at day 7, which suggested the possibility of a weekly interval between treatments.
engagement.confidence_note: Konkle 2020 read at abstract level (NEJM paywalled); model side from Chhabra 2020 full text (PMC7180082). Paired by the drafter, not stated in the trial paper.

engagement.note: Liver biopsies 2.6-4.1 years after valoctocogene showed hepatocyte transduction, circular episomes and FVIII-SQ RNA with the same dose trends as mice and macaques.

engagement.judgement: Explicit tissue-level comparison by the sponsor; strengthens the 2020 protein-modality match on the same track rather than opening a new status. Registry date is the phase 1/2 results posting (NCT02576795).

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 35821634, epub 2022-07-12); University of Florida / Indiana University, AAV8-hFVIII, not a member product.

engagement.judgement: Status retro, never same (decision 10): the clinic already knew FVIII fell. Placed in engagement because the retrodicted quantity is the transgene-protein readout over time; no prospective prediction from this model has been tested in patients.
engagement.note: The model reproduces the clinical pattern: FVIII protein falls over time without inhibitors despite persistent transgene and mRNA, with ER stress in some animals.

engagement.confidence_note: Registry record only (results posted 2025-08-22; trial terminated for rollover, 3 enrolled, 2 did not complete). The US label restricts to antibody-negative patients by the AAV5 DetectCDx companion diagnostic, but the regulator relied on trial exclusion, not on this model in lieu of a trial.
engagement.judgement: Direction agrees (antibody-positive recipients under-express) but n=3 and the registry gives counts, not levels; low confidence rather than untested because a comparison can be made.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 28056565, epub 2017-01-05). No FDA/EMA review exists for this unapproved product.

dose.note: Mouse dose-response was the class's exposure model; dogs received lower doses of canine FVIII and were never dose-matched to patients.
dose.quote: After intraportal vein injection of these vectors in hemophilia-A mice, therapeutic to superphysiologic levels of active FVIII were achieved in plasma in a dose-dependent manner.
dose.judgement: Opening entry for the gene-therapy strip.

dose.note: 6e13 vg/kg, the mouse-supported dose, gave therapeutic FVIII in patients; mice reached 380% at steady state, patients plateaued at 104%, a 3.7-fold drop.
dose.short: Dose reached and worked; mouse 3.7x high
dose.quote: This results in approximately 3.7-fold drop of FVIII expression of BMN 270 from mouse to human.
dose.confidence_note: Full text via PMC5835117; the sponsor's own mouse-to-human comparison. Online 2017-12-14, print 2018.
dose.magnitude_basis: steady-state plasma FVIII at 6e13 vg/kg: 380% of normal in mice vs 104% plateau in phase 1/2 patients
dose.population: Severe hemophilia A (FVIII ≤1 IU/dL), adults without anti-AAV5 antibodies
dose.judgement: Judgement call. v2 scored this contra; under v3 'reached, drug worked' is same with the magnitude recorded. Direction held at 6e13 vg/kg, but 6e12 and 2e13 vg/kg gave ≤3 IU/dL in patients (Rangarajan 2017, 10.1056/NEJMoa1708483), so the clinical dose came from escalation, not from the mouse number. Macaques (n=2/dose) lost expression to anti-hFVIII antibodies and could not set a target. Decision 16: the model stated a tolerated margin (no ALT rise in mice to 2e14 or monkeys to 3.6e13 vg/kg; FDA mouse toxicology mortality only at ≥6.53e13 vg/kg) and patients were dosed to 6e13 without that toxicity, so margin_stated is true; the ALT rise the model never predicted is counted once, in safety.

dose.note: BIVV001 (efanesoctocog alfa) half-life was 25-31 h in mice and 33-34 h in monkeys, a 3-4x extension over rFVIII.
dose.quote: Plasma FVIII half-life after BIVV001 administration in mice and monkeys was 25 to 31 hours and 33 to 34 hours, respectively, representing a three- to fourfold increase in FVIII half-life.
dose.confidence_note: Full text via PMC7180082 (key points and abstract read).
dose.judgement: Opens the protein strip at the first member-specific model use I could verify; F8-knockout mice were used for earlier rFVIII products, so model_first_use_year keeps the track's 2003 proxy.

dose.note: In patients BIVV001 half-life was 37.6-42.5 h vs 9.1-13.2 h for rFVIII, the 3-4x extension mice and monkeys predicted.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Konkle 2020; quote is the first clause of a longer sentence, elided at the semicolon. Paired by the drafter with Chhabra 2020.

dose.population: Severe hemophilia A (FVIII ≤1 IU/dL), previously treated adults

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 34652966, epub 2021-12-08). Patient dose range from the 2024 Blood Advances meta-analysis table (NCT03588299: 5e12, 1e13, 2e13, 4e13).
dose.judgement: Dose cell opens at the MED study rather than 2017 because the earlier papers set no exposure target.

dose.model: FVIII-knockout mice + cynomolgus macaques given AAVhu37.E03.TTR.hFVIIIco-SQ (BAY 2599023 / DTX201, peboctocogene camaparvovec)

efficacy.note: AAV2-FVIII corrected the bleeding diathesis in F8-knockout mice: all treated mice survived tail clipping.
efficacy.short: Mice survive tail clip after AAV-FVIII

efficacy.judgement: Opening entry for the mouse track.

efficacy.model: Hemophilia A dogs (Chapel Hill / Queen's colonies)

efficacy.judgement: Dogs received canine FVIII at ~1e13 vg/kg, never a member product; model_filed false because the Roctavian SBRA lists only mice and nonhuman primates.

efficacy.model: Hemophilia A dogs (Chapel Hill / Queen's colonies)
efficacy.note: AAV8-cFVIII dogs showed >90% fewer bleeds over 24 dog-years with stable expression and no lasting inhibitor; the field's durability prediction.

efficacy.judgement: Strengthens the untested dog opening with the specific prediction later tested: durable expression and bleed reduction. Nguyen 2021 (10.1038/s41587-020-0741-7) extended the same dogs to 10 years at 1.9-11.3% FVIII.

efficacy.model: Hemophilia A dogs (Chapel Hill / Queen's colonies)
efficacy.note: Dogs held FVIII for 10 years; valoctocogene recipients lost about half their expression from year 1 to 2, called unexpected given the dogs.
efficacy.quote: These results were unexpected given observations … from studies in large-animal models of hemophilia A that showed durable factor VIII transgene-derived expression for 10 years.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text via PMC8672712 author manuscript; quote elided with an ellipsis from a 48-word sentence that also cites hemophilia B trials. The miss is on durability, not on the 1-year primary endpoint.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: durability: dogs stable ≥10 years vs ~50% loss of FVIII activity from year 1 to year 2 after valoctocogene (Pasi 2020, Mahlangu 2023)

patient_trials.quote: In patients with severe hemophilia A, valoctocogene roxaparvovec treatment provided endogenous factor VIII production and significantly reduced bleeding and factor VIII concentrate use relative to factor VIII prophylaxis.
Among the 16 participants in whom factor VIII expression was maintained outside the capsid immune response window, 12 were followed for more than 2 years and had apparent multiyear stable expression.
The AFFINE study achieved its primary objective of non-inferiority, as well as superiority, of total annualized bleeding rate (ABR) from Week 12 through at least 15 months of follow up post-infusion

efficacy.population: Severe hemophilia A (FVIII ≤1 IU/dL), adults without anti-AAV antibodies
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call. Every trial's bleeding endpoint fell as the dogs predicted (GENEr8-1 ABR -84.5% at 2 years; AFFINE met ABR non-inferiority and superiority per Pfizer press release 2024-07-24 and registry results 2025-08-17), and SPK-8011 matched dog durability; a reader weighting the pre-specified 1-year primary endpoint would score same + partial. I score contra because George 2021 is a tier-1 stated comparison that the dogs' durability prediction failed for valoctocogene, the FDA clinical memo records 'no steady-state FVIII activity' with continuing decline, and one drug's contra beats another's same on a track. The dogs were dosed with canine FVIII (AAV2/6/8/9, ~1e13 vg/kg), never a member product, so product_in_model is false.

efficacy.note: GENEr8-1 met its primary endpoint: FVIII activity rose 41.9 IU/dL at weeks 49-52 after 6e13 vg/kg valoctocogene, with bleeding and factor use reduced.
efficacy.quote: In patients with severe hemophilia A, valoctocogene roxaparvovec treatment provided endogenous factor VIII production and significantly reduced bleeding and factor VIII concentrate use relative to factor VIII prophylaxis.
efficacy.confidence_note: Ozelo 2022 read at abstract level (NEJM paywalled); paired by the drafter with Bunting 2018 (mice expressed FVIII-SQ and corrected clotting).
efficacy.magnitude_basis: FVIII expression and bleeding correction: mice 380% FVIII at 12 weeks vs patients +41.9 IU/dL at 1 year; different endpoints, direction only

patient_trials.quote: The mean annualized treated bleeding rate decreased by 84.5% from baseline
Factor VIII activity levels remained at 3 IU or less per deciliter in the recipients of the low or intermediate dose.

The later decline is scored on this track by the 2025 BAX 888 entry.

efficacy.note: XTEND-1 met its primary endpoint: once-weekly efanesoctocog alfa gave mean ABR 0.71, superior to prior prophylaxis, as 4x hemostatic cover in mice predicted.

patient_trials.quote: In group A (133 patients), the median annualized bleeding rate was 0 (interquartile range, 0 to 1.04), and the estimated mean annualized bleeding rate was 0.71 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.52 to 0.97).

efficacy.judgement: Protein modality, pooled on the mouse track; strengthens the 2022 match.

efficacy.note: TAK-754 (BAX 888) gave long-term stable FVIII in tolerant human-FVIII mice; all four dosed patients lost FVIII expression within 12 months and the program stopped.
efficacy.short: Mouse-stable BAX 888 lost in all patients
efficacy.quote: All participants developed mild transient transaminase elevation and subsequent loss of FVIII expression within the first 12 months of treatment despite use of glucocorticoids.
efficacy.confidence_note: Chapin 2024 (Haemophilia, online 2024-12-23) read in full text via PMC11780198; model side is the TAK-754 preclinical report (Mol Ther Methods Clin Dev, online 2025-01-28), abstract level. Year is 2025, when both sides were public; the mouse work predates the trial.
efficacy.reason: Mouse-stable expression lost in every patient
efficacy.magnitude_basis: durability of transgene FVIII: long-term stable in tolerant hFVIII-transgenic mice vs complete loss within 12 months in 4/4 patients

patient_trials.quote: Sustained FVIII expression remains a challenge in haemophilia A AAV gene therapy trials.

At the highest dose level (3 × 10¹³ vg/kg; n = 5), the mean circulating FVIII activity level at week 52 was 42.6% (range, 7.8%-122.3%), and at week 104 it was 25.4% (range, 0.9%-71.6%) based on a chromogenic assay.

efficacy.judgement: Judgement call. The phase 1/2 primary endpoint was safety, so endogenous FVIII activity is the proof-of-concept gate. The mouse cannot mount the capsid-directed response blamed for the loss, which argues for leniency, but the model's stated prediction (long-term stable expression) failed outright for a member drug, and the same decline (valoctocogene ~50%/year, giroctocogene 42.6% to 25.4% from week 52 to 104) recurs across the class; the mouse track therefore ends contra. Pairing made by the drafter; neither paper states the comparison.

safety.note: Macaques at 1e13-3.6e13 vg/kg and mice at up to 2e14 vg/kg showed no ALT/AST rise, no caspase-3 activation and no hepatocyte ER stress.

safety.judgement: Platform (AAV capsid) harm strip, so split by modality. The FDA mouse toxicology also recorded mortality with cardiac fibrosis/necrosis only at ≥6.53e13 vg/kg, above the 6e13 clinical dose, so that stated margin held and is not scored.

safety.judgement: Judgement call. A macaque can show a transaminase rise and the sponsor measured ALT/AST in both species without seeing one, so the model's silence is contradicted on a harm the species could show (v3 safety rule); v2 left this untested because no source states the comparison, which v3 rule 1 now allows as a hatched pairing. The harm is counted once, here, because the model never predicted it (decision 16). Fong 2022's narrow ER-stress match in five biopsies does not reverse the track.

safety.note: In the phase 3 package 81% of patients had ALT above normal and 87% of the efficacy population needed immunosuppression; hepatotoxicity is labelled.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 32775496, epub 2020-07-09). Whether this study is in the BLA pharmacology section could not be checked: the SBRA nonclinical text is partly redacted.
safety.judgement: Same model system, now run with the clinical construct; prediction for patients: no ER stress at the clinical promoter/dose.
safety.note: BioMarin's own AAV5-hFVIII-SQ mice: ER-stress markers rose only with a stronger promoter at the top dose, not with valoctocogene's HLP promoter.
safety.short: Product's promoter: no ER stress in mice
safety.quote: For 100ATGB, liver hFVIII-SQ protein accumulated dose dependently, with increased expression of ER stress markers at the highest dose, suggesting hepatocytes reached or exceeded their capacity to fold/secrete hFVIII-SQ.
safety.model: Hemophilia A mice, hepatic AAV-FVIII overexpression (ER-stress / unfolded-protein-response model)

safety.magnitude_basis: hepatocyte ER-stress markers (GRP78/BiP) in FVIII-expressing cells: none in mice with the clinical promoter, none in 5 patient biopsies
safety.confidence_note: Full text via PMC9018415; Fong 2022 cites Lange 2016 and its own mice but does not set them beside the biopsies, so paired by me. The mouse harm was conditional on >200% FVIII or a stronger promoter, conditions patients never reached (peak ~60-100%, lower at biopsy), so only the no-stress half of the prediction is tested; n=5, single late time point.
safety.judgement: Scored same, not contra/opposite: the model never predicted ER stress at the levels patients reached. A contra would need patients at supraphysiologic FVIII with stress, or stress at therapeutic levels.
safety.note: Liver biopsies 2.6-4.1 years after valoctocogene: FVIII-SQ-expressing hepatocytes showed no GRP78 rise and no ER stress, as the mice predicted at therapeutic levels.
safety.quote: Histopathology revealed no dysplasia, architectural distortion, fibrosis or chronic inflammation, and no endoplasmic reticulum stress was detected in hepatocytes expressing hFVIII-SQ protein.
safety.reason: No ER stress at therapeutic FVIII, as predicted
safety.model: Hemophilia A mice, hepatic AAV-FVIII overexpression (ER-stress / unfolded-protein-response model)

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 34652966). The trial's primary outcome is adverse events, but no results are posted and no label or review exists.
safety.judgement: Untested; a mouse cannot show capsid T-cell hepatitis, so its silence there would not be a miss even once patient data appear.
safety.note: Mouse toxicology of the clinical candidate: no transaminase rise or vector-related histology up to 1e13 GC/kg; patient safety (primary endpoint of NCT03588299) not posted.
safety.quote: We observed no vector-related gross or histological findings.
safety.model: FVIII-knockout mice + cynomolgus macaques given AAVhu37.E03.TTR.hFVIIIco-SQ (BAY 2599023 / DTX201, peboctocogene camaparvovec)
